story_theme_en: The teacher divided a banana cake equally among 4 students. Mali received 1 piece and Lin received 1 piece. How much of the whole cake did each student get? And which fraction is greater?

think_story_en: Cake divided into 4 equal parts. Mali gets 1/4. Lin gets 1/4. 1/4 = 1/4, both get the same amount. 3/4 of the cake is left over.

visual_blocks.question: A pizza is divided into 6 equal slices. Mark eats 2 slices. What fraction of the pizza did Mark eat?

data.question: A pizza is divided into 6 equal slices. Mark eats 2 slices. What fraction of the pizza did Mark eat?
data.explanation: Divided into 6, ate 2 slices = 2/6 of the pizza

data.description: The fraction 2/4 simplifies to 1/2 by dividing both numerator and denominator by 2

explanation_steps_en: A fraction has 2 parts: numerator (top) tells how many parts you have; denominator (bottom) tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into.
Cake divided into 4 parts = denominator 4. Mali gets 1 part = numerator 1. So Mali gets 1/4 of the cake.
When comparing fractions with the same denominator, look at the numerator. Larger numerator = larger fraction.
1/4 and 1/4: numerators are equal, so both students get the same amount.
common_mistakes_en: Thinking a fraction with bigger numbers is always greater without checking the denominator.
Forgetting that fractions must represent equal parts.
hints_en: Remember: Denominator (bottom) = how many parts it is divided into. Numerator (top) = how many parts are taken.
Draw a circle divided into equal parts and shade the parts you need.
When denominators are the same, compare numerators only.

explanation_en: A fraction has a numerator (top) and denominator (bottom). Denominator = number of equal parts the whole is divided into. Numerator = number of those parts we have. When denominators are equal, compare numerators. Simplify by dividing both by the same number.
